text: Every single role you defined back in Desktop sits completely inert and does absolutely nothing on its own, until someone actually gets assigned to it — and that assignment step only ever happens here, in the Power BI service itself.

Hover directly over the semantic model in its workspace to reveal a More options menu — genuinely easy to miss the very first time through, since it only shows up the moment your mouse actually hovers there.

Select Security from that menu. If your semantic model has no RLS roles defined yet back in Desktop, this Security option genuinely won't even appear here at all — go back and finish Lesson 80 first if that's the case.

Add anyone at all by their email address, including external guest users from outside your own organization — but never a group that was created entirely inside Power BI itself. Distribution groups, mail-enabled groups, and Microsoft Entra security groups all work perfectly fine here. Microsoft 365 groups specifically do not, and can never be added to any RLS role at all.

Each individual role shows its current member count directly in parentheses right next to its own name — a genuinely fast sanity check that tells you exactly how many people are assigned, without ever needing to open the role itself to check.

Roles are now properly assigned, with real people attached to them. Lesson 82 covers actually validating that everything truly works as expected, plus the dynamic pattern that adapts automatically to whoever happens to be signed in at any given moment.
